Test uses a typical large vertex count and a negative weight but does not systematically exercise boundary values (zero, empty graph, negative/maximum indices) or document boundary intent.
The test is short and self-contained (< 10 lines) with no duplicated setup across multiple tests; there are no helper methods needed for this single case.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test is small (< 20 lines), linear, and contains no loops or conditional logic, keeping cyclomatic complexity low.
The test performs multiple specific assertions (assertNotSame and assertEquals for vertex counts) which verify several properties (distinct instance and vertex counts).
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods; the test appears active and runnable.
The class-level Javadoc includes explicit traceability information: 'Traceability: REQ-GRAFO-01..09', linking tests to requirements.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit test focused on functional behavior; there are no performance or security test expectations and no timeout-based performance assertions required beyond the test timeout.
The method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome; it does not follow descriptive naming conventions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: Presence of EvoSuite runner and a numbered test name (test8) indicate generated/origin artifacts and non-minimal naming patterns, suggesting remnants of auto-generated tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains only a minimal, single happy-path test and lacks Given-When-Then structure or multiple scenarios suggesting test-first design or prioritized coverage.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public Grafo APIs and does not access private fields or use reflection; thus it focuses on observable behavior and is not tightly coupled to implementation internals.

The test uses specific assertion methods (assertNotSame and assertEquals) rather than generic assertTrue; multiple properties are asserted. Although messages are missing, assertions are specific and meaningful.
The class includes a concise explanatory Javadoc comment that explains traceability and purpose; there are no excessive or commented-out lines inside the test method.
No sources of non-determinism are used (no Random, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies). The test uses only deterministic operations.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local objects and does not create files, modify static variables, or persist external state; no cleanup is required.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: Although a UnitTest marker interface exists, the test methods are not annotated with @Category or @Tag; there is no categorization present to enable selective runs.

The test performs multiple distinct actions: insereAresta (setup) and retiraAresta (act) and also asserts numVertices. It effectively tests multiple behaviors in one method rather than a single focused Arrange-Act-Assert, so it is not atomic.
The test uses only local variables and does not rely on static or shared mutable state. No setup/teardown annotations are required for this single method.
